Altercation

/awl-ter-KAY-shuhn/ - the stress falls on KAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Altercation means a noisy, heated dispute.

An altercation over the bill flared at the next table, and the whole cafe went quiet to listen.

Worked Example

Somewhere over Nebraska, two passengers discovered one overhead bin and two roller bags. Voices rose; an elbow was thrown wide; a flight attendant arrived with the practiced calm of someone who has separated grown adults before. By the time the seatbelt light chimed, both bags were stowed, both men were seated rows apart, and the whole affair had lasted four minutes.

Altercation is the exact word for that four minutes: a dispute, a fight — loud, abrupt, and over. It names the flare-up itself, not what led there and not what lingers after. A grievance can smolder for years; an altercation is the moment it sparks, and when the shouting stops, the altercation is finished.

How Altercation Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

quarrel

quarrel: an angry back-and-forth that can happen quietly, at any length

squabble

squabble: a petty flare-up over something small

Antonyms

truce

truce: an agreed pause in fighting

reconciliation

reconciliation: the mending that puts a fight to rest

How Strong Is It? — disagreement → altercation → brawl

disagreement vs. altercation

disagreement vs. altercation: A disagreement can stay perfectly civil — two views that simply differ; an altercation has already turned loud and heated.

brawl vs. altercation

brawl vs. altercation: A brawl goes past altercation: fists out, furniture over, a fight that needs more than a stern word to stop.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — alterc

Root — alterc: to trade sharp words (from alter, "other")

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: act of

Put it together

Put it together: Alterc- (from Latin alter, "other") + -ation (act of) = an act of going at one another. Latin altercari meant to trade words with the other party, turn and turn about — and an altercation still moves like that: sharp words batted back and forth between two people until someone steps in.

Use the root in a new word: alter

Use the root in a new word: alter: When you alter a plan, you make it other than it was.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / news-report

Altercation is the reporter's word for a dispute that flared — loud, brief, and usually over by the time anyone writes it down. It names one incident; for the standing bad feeling between people, this unit offers hostility, and for hatred that has settled in for years, enmity. If it came to blows and rolled on the floor, brawl says so.
